title: Your Work Rhythm
text: You've found your feet at {employer}. Your manager calls you 'high potential', which is how they say 'stay late'. The next ten years will be shaped by one quiet decision: how many hours you give.

variants.text: Thesis defended, badge printed: you start at {employer} with a doctorate and a backlog of sleep. Your manager calls you 'high potential', which is how they say 'stay late'. The next ten years will be shaped by one quiet decision: how many hours you give.

speaker: first_manager

hints: Bertrand, the first manager, is in the room and says 'no pressure'.
This is the 'extreme time' choice: hours shape promotions, health and lifespan.

footprint.label: Grind lifestyle: taxis, takeaways, last-minute flights (design estimate)

effects.text: Your calendar becomes a game of falling blocks you are losing gracefully.
You leave at 6:30PM. Some colleagues look at you like you're defecting. You are.

choices.label: A four-day week
choices.hint: Fridays are yours, raises less so

effects.text: Friday becomes market day, sport day, nap day. Your career slows down. You speed up.
You hand in your notice with a speech you rehearsed in the shower.

title: Back on the Market
text: A year of coffees, interviews and 'tell me about a time you failed'. Your inbox fills up again, and this time you know what the beanbags mean. Who gets the next ten years?

hints: Reference the old employer the player just left.

title: Life at Home
text: Thirty. Your friends' group chat has turned into a slideshow of weddings, babies and sourdough. Everyone at family dinners asks the same question, with the same face. What does your life look like at home?

variants.text: Thirty. Remember the person from that 3AM conversation outside the sète? You never really stopped talking, and lately Noa has started asking the very big question, gently: what does home look like for you?

ai.tone: tender, funny, never judgemental about any family shape
hints: If flag met_3am, the partner is Noa, the person from the 3AM conversation: reference that night.
Never use gendered pronouns for the player or the partner.

effects.text: Your kids think a tablet is something you take for a headache. You are exhausted and weirdly proud.
Dinner is quiet. Very quiet. Three faces lit blue from below.

choices.label: A partner, no kids
choices.hint: Freedom, long brunches, maybe a cat

effects.text: Two careers, one cat, zero bedtime stories. Sundays are long and lovely.
Your flat is spotless and silent. Your career is grateful. Your plants, less so.

title: Your Flagship Project
text: Thirty-three, and {employer} hands you the project everyone will remember you for. The budget is real, the deadline is not. The big question in the room: how much AI, and at what cost?

variants.text: Thirty-three, and {employer} hands you the new AI trading system: the project everyone will remember you for. The budget is real, the deadline is not. How much AI, and at what cost?
Thirty-three, and {employer} puts you in charge of a client's 'AI transformation programme', eighty slides deep. The fees are real, the deadline is not. How much AI do you actually recommend?
Thirty-three, and {employer} gives you the next big model: the launch everyone will remember you for. The compute budget is real, the deadline is not. How much AI, and at what cost?
Thirty-three, and your lab at {employer} gets the grant for its flagship model. The compute is shared, the deadline is a conference. How big do you go, and what do you point it at?
Thirty-three, and {employer} asks you to build the model that will steer hospital budgets for a decade. The stakes are real, the data is messy. How much AI do you put in it?
Thirty-three, and {employer} asks you to draft the technical annex of an international AI treaty. Every delegation has a lobbyist. What do you write into it?
Thirty-three, and {employer} gives you the AI programme for its grid and its sites. The budget is real, the emissions are too. How much AI, and pointed at what?
Thirty-three, and {employer} names you lead of its group-wide AI strategy. Every division wants its own ChatGBT. What do you actually build?
Thirty-three, and {employer} finally gets a grant for a digital tool for its field teams. The budget is small, the need is huge. How much AI do you put in it?
Thirty-three, and your startup's next funding round depends on its core product. The investors want 'more AI'. The runway wants less spending. What do you build?
Thirty-three, and the farm co-op wants to 'do something with AI' after a neighbour's drone demo. The budget is a jar of coins and a grant form. What do you build, if anything?

hints: Make the project concrete for the player's path and employer.
Facts available: frontier training around 42 GWh; frugal AI (AFNOR Spec 2314); AI could cut around 5% of energy emissions.
Never preach: scaling is genuinely exciting.

effects.text: The launch trends for two days. The data centre's electricity bill trends for two years.

footprint.label: Frugal model, measured and disclosed (work footprint)

effects.text: You cut the model size by ten and the accuracy by two percent. The CFO cries tears of joy.

choices.label: AI for climate or health
choices.hint: Point the tool at a real problem
choices.lockedReason: Requires the Impact asso, or a research, NGO, policy, energy or strategy role

footprint.label: Applied AI for climate or health (work footprint)

effects.text: Your model helps a grid run on more wind and a hospital plan its heatwave beds. Not glamorous. Measurable.
A linear regression and one good chart do the job. Two people in the meeting look betrayed.

title: Your Online Presence
text: Thirty-six. Slacker at work, the family group on FaceBuk and an algorithm that knows you better than your parents do. A colleague with a big following says you 'should really build your brand'. Time to decide your online life for good.

variants.text: Thirty-six. You've been posting daily since Year 1 and your follower count has its own personality. A brand agency wants you full-time. Your friends want you back at dinner. Time to decide your online life for good.
Thirty-six. You've kept your phone on a short leash since Year 1, but work now lives on Slacker and your colleague says you 'should really build your brand'. Time to decide your online life for good.

hints: This replaces the Year 1 phone habit for the rest of the life.
A big audience means a big influence footprint (watch time you generate).

choices.label: Build a personal brand
choices.hint: Hours a day, a big audience

effects.text: Your LinkedOut post about 'five lessons from failure' gets two million views. You failed at nothing that week.

choices.label: Online as needed
choices.hint: A couple of hours, mostly useful

effects.text: You post twice a year: one job update, one sunset. Perfectly balanced.
Goodbye InstaGran, goodbye TikTac. Week one, your thumb twitches. Week two, you read a novel. Week three, you call your grandmother.

title: Mid-Career Crossroads
text: Forty. Your company offers you a long-term track, a friend pitches a startup over dinner, and a slower life keeps whispering from the countryside. Your eighteen-year-old self would have opinions. What's the plan for the next twenty years?

variants.text: Forty, and your old job now runs on a server somewhere. The severance was decent, the silence is loud, and nobody in your old field hires humans for it any more. What's the plan for the next twenty years?

Forty, between two chapters. A friend pitches a startup over dinner, a cooperative needs hands, an NGO needs a director. Your eighteen-year-old self would have opinions. What's the plan for the next twenty years?

hints: If flag ai_job_loss, going back to the old job is greyed: the player cannot go back to that field.
If flag founder later, the AI names the startup.

effects.text: You get a bigger office and a smaller window. Five years blur into quarterly reviews, and your badge photo will not be updated until retirement.
You sign up for ten more years and a standing desk you will never stand at. The first five go by in a blink.

choices.label: Go back to your old job
choices.hint: That desk has a server on it now
choices.lockedReason: Locked: that job went to an AI in the shock

effects.text: Your salary halves. Your Sunday-evening dread disappears entirely.
You buy a domain name at 1AM. Then a second one, just in case.
You trade the commute for a vegetable garden and the notifications for birdsong. Your old colleagues call it a phase.

choices.label: Start over in a new field

effects.text: You rewrite your CV from scratch. The first line is the hardest.

title: Your Startup
text: You've got a co-founder, a domain name and a whiteboard covered in arrows. All that's missing is a sector, a product and roughly two million euros. Where do you place your bet?

hints: The AI will name the startup, its product, investor and rival after this choice.

title: A Second First Job
text: Forty, with a fresh CV and old instincts. Recruiters in other fields are surprisingly curious about someone who has already lived through one revolution. Who gets your second career?

hints: The old field is banned: greyed offers say no one there hires after the AI shock.
